title: How a Large Language Model Predicts the Next Token

sections.subtitle: Text becomes tokens
sections.description:
A language model never sees a sentence. It sees a sequence of tokens — small chunks of text mapped to integer IDs. The same sentence can become different token sequences depending on the tokenizer.

Token counts matter because context windows, pricing, and latency are all measured in tokens.

consoleBlock.py:
text = "AI learning hub"
tokens = text.lower().split()

print("tokens:", tokens)
print("count:", len(tokens))

sections.subtitle: From logits to probabilities
sections.description:
For every position, the model produces a score (a logit) for every token in its vocabulary. Softmax turns those scores into a probability distribution. The next token is sampled from that distribution.

A greedy decoder always picks the highest-probability token. Sampling adds controlled randomness.

python.title: Compute a softmax distribution
python.code:
import math

logits = {"learning": 2.4, "systems": 1.1, "models": 0.6, "other": 0.2}
total = sum(math.exp(value) for value in logits.values())

for token, score in logits.items():
    probability = math.exp(score) / total
    bar = "#" * int(probability * 40)
    print(f"{token:>9} {probability:6.3f} {bar}")

sections.subtitle: Temperature reshapes the distribution
sections.description:
Temperature divides the logits before softmax. Low temperature makes the model more deterministic; high temperature makes it more exploratory.

Use low temperature for extraction and code. Use higher temperature for brainstorming — and always evaluate the result.

consoleBlock.py:
import math

def softmax(logits, temperature=1.0):
    scaled = [value / temperature for value in logits]
    top = max(scaled)
    exps = [math.exp(value - top) for value in scaled]
    total = sum(exps)
    return [value / total for value in exps]

logits = [2.4, 1.1, 0.6, 0.2]

for temperature in [0.2, 1.0, 2.0]:
    probs = softmax(logits, temperature)
    print(f"T={temperature:<4} " + " ".join(f"{p:.3f}" for p in probs))
